title: How UX design works: usability, process and ethics

say: How UX design works: usability, process and ethics.
This is the video for module 1 of UX Design Fundamentals.
User experience, or UX, is everything a person feels and does while using a product, from finding it to deciding whether to come back.

say: User interface, or UI, is only the part you can see and touch: buttons, colours, fonts and screens.
A beautiful screen can still give a bad experience if the button you need is hidden or the words are confusing.

say: Usability has five parts, and you will use these words for the rest of the course.
Learnability. Can a new user send money on a wallet app on day one without help?

panel.heading: The five components of usability
items: Learnability: easy on day one?
Efficiency: how fast once she knows it?
Memorability: can she still use it after weeks away?
Errors: how many, how serious, how easy to fix?
Satisfaction: calm or anxious while using it?

say: Efficiency. Once she knows the app, does buying airtime take 4 taps or 12?

say: Here is a real problem. Amaka in Onitsha sends money to her supplier with a mobile banking app.
After her PIN, the screen spins for about 40 seconds, then returns home with no message at all.
Her first transfer is 25,000 naira. She checks her balance, but the debit has not shown yet.
So she tries again. Both transfers go through.
She has sent 50,000 naira instead of 25,000.
The fix is not a new colour. Show a clear processing, do not retry message, a transaction reference, and a warning about repeat transfers.
Designers follow a process so decisions come from evidence, not personal taste. It is called design thinking.
First, empathise. For example, Funke phones 6 members of her learning network who cannot find their certificates.

panel.heading: Design thinking in five stages
items: Empathise: observe and interview real users
Define: write a clear problem statement
Ideate: list many ideas before choosing
Prototype: build a cheap, quick version
Test: watch real users try it, then improve

say: Second, define. She writes: members cannot find their certificate because it sits under Settings, which they do not link with achievements.

say: This is the rule. A weak statement says, we need a new menu. A strong one says which user struggles, with what task, and why.

The process is a loop. Testing often sends you back to define the problem more sharply, and that is normal.

say: When you interview people, you collect personal information, so treat it with care.
Always get informed consent. She must understand what you are doing, why, how long it takes, what you will record, and that she can stop at any time.

cards.d: Explain the purpose, the time, what you record, and that she can stop at any time.
Use codes like P1, P2 instead of names. Keep notes locked and delete them when done.
No PINs, passwords, BVN or account numbers, even in a test. Use fake data instead.

say: Nigeria's Data Protection Act 2023 sets rules for personal data. Follow the basic principles: collect only what you need, keep it safe, and delete it when you are done.

say: Never ask for bank PINs, passwords, BVN or account numbers, even in a test prototype.
Meet people in public or familiar places, or by phone, and tell someone where you are going.

say: For example, Zainab tells a tailor in Kaduna that the interview takes about 20 minutes, and that she is testing ideas, not testing her.
Check these five things before every session. Purpose explained. Time stated. Permission to record. Right to stop. And names removed from your notes.

panel.heading: Before any research session
items: Purpose explained clearly
Time needed stated
Recording permission asked
Right to stop explained
Names removed from notes

say: To remember. UX is the whole experience, and UI is only the visible part. Learn the five usability components.
Follow the design thinking loop, keep your project small, and always protect the people who help you.

panel.heading: Remember
items: UX is the whole experience; UI is the visible part
Five parts: learn, speed, memory, errors, satisfaction
Empathise, define, ideate, prototype, test, then repeat
Choose one small, real project you can reach users for
Consent first, and never collect PINs or BVNs
